name: Oak Brook
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Oak Brook, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Oak Brook, IL: Winter Lights at Central Park, The Drake tree lighting, Santa at Oakbrook Center, Graue Mill and Santa trains nearby.
lede: Oak Brook does Christmas with a free half-mile walk of lights in Central Park, a carol-filled tree lighting at The Drake Oak Brook and photos with Santa on The Lawn at Oakbrook Center. Add a Victorian holiday morning at Graue Mill and families have a full season close to home.
celebrates: Oak Brook's biggest holiday tradition is Winter Lights at Central Park, a free half-mile loop that the Oak Brook Park District runs every night from late November into early January. Families walk or roll past dancing trees, rainbow arches, twirling icicles, butterflies and musical hearts, and each evening starts with a calm sensory-friendly half hour. On select nights the Cocoa Cabin at Central Park West sells hot chocolate and cookies. The Drake Oak Brook hotel invites the public to its annual tree lighting with carolers and a canned food drive. Oakbrook Center offers photos with Santa on The Lawn, and Graue Mill recreates an 1850s Victorian holiday with readings from A Christmas Carol.
lastyear: Winter Lights at Central Park ran every night from November 21, 2025, into early January, and the park district called it a record-breaking season. Its AI trail counter logged more than 70,500 visits, and many guests came back more than once. Last season was also the first with the daily sensory-friendly time, when the lights stayed still and the music was off from 4 to 4:30 pm. The Cocoa Cabin sold over 4,400 cookies and 6,500 cups of hot cocoa, its best sales ever, and visitors gave more than $7,500 to People's Resource Center and the park district foundation.
facts: Oak Brook became a village on February 21, 1958, when it covered one square mile and had only 103 residents. Oakbrook Center opened in 1962 on a 150 acre farm that Marshall Field and Company bought in 1955. The Drake Oak Brook was built in 1961 as an extension of The Drake Hotel in downtown Chicago and has hosted guests such as Frank Sinatra. Graue Mill on Salt Creek is even older: it opened in April 1852, and its four 1 ton grinding stones were shipped over from France.
trains: Oak Brook sits between Hinsdale and Elmhurst, and both towns have Metra stations. Hinsdale station, at 21 E. Hinsdale Ave., is on the BNSF line between Aurora and Chicago Union Station. Elmhurst station, at 1st Street and York Road, is on the Union Pacific West line to Ogilvie Transportation Center. For a Christmas ride, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, where Santa rides along with a light show and holiday songs. The Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express on a decorated 1950s trolley, where Santa visits each family.
train_links: Ride the Happy Holiday Railway with Santa from the historic East Union Depot in Union.
Santa's Trolley Express runs on a decorated 1950s trolley along the Fox River in South Elgin.
traditions: A free, one-way half-mile loop of lights on a paved path that works for strollers and wheelchairs, with leashed dogs welcome.
From 4 to 4:30 pm each evening the Winter Lights hold still and the music is off, a calmer start the park district added in 2025.
On select nights Central Park West serves hot chocolate and cookies, and some nights raise money for groups like the Oak Brook Historical Society.
A free public lighting with carolers, hot chocolate and cookies, plus a canned food drive for a local food pantry.
Mistletoe and Merriment at Graue Mill
A Victorian holiday morning at the 1852 mill with corn grinding, readings from A Christmas Carol and holiday crafts.
Holiday Express to the North Pole
The park district takes families by coach bus from the Family Recreation Center to meet Santa at Central Park West, with crafts and a bounce house.
kidfact: Graue Mill in Oak Brook first started grinding grain with water from Salt Creek in 1852. Each of its four big grinding stones weighs about a ton, and they came all the way from France.
faq: Is Winter Lights at Central Park free?

Yes. Admission and parking are free, and donations along the path help People's Resource Center and the Oak Brook Park District Foundation. The paved half-mile loop is one way and accessible for strollers and wheelchairs, and leashed dogs are welcome. On mild nights the lots can fill, so the park district asks visitors to use the overflow parking on its map and never park on the grass.
What is the sensory-friendly time at Winter Lights?

Every evening from 4 to 4:30 pm, before the full show starts, all blinking and moving lights stay still and the music is silenced. The park district added this calmer half hour in 2025 so children and adults who are sensitive to flashing lights or loud sound can enjoy the walk too. The animated displays begin at 4:30 pm.
Can anyone go to the tree lighting at The Drake Oak Brook?

Yes. The Drake Oak Brook says its annual tree lighting is free and open to the public. Carolers sing holiday favorites, and the hotel serves hot chocolate and cookies. Guests are asked to bring a canned good for the hotel's annual food drive, which supports a local food pantry, so it is an easy way to show kids how to give back.
Where can kids see Santa in Oak Brook?

Oakbrook Center offers photos with Santa on The Lawn, and families can reserve a time online. The Oak Brook Park District also runs the Holiday Express, a coach bus ride from the Family Recreation Center to meet Santa at the North Pole, which is Central Park West, with crafts, a bounce house and light refreshments. Holiday Express riders over age 2 must register.
What happens at Graue Mill at Christmas?

Graue Mill and Museum holds Mistletoe and Merriment at the Mill, which recreates an 1850s Victorian holiday with corn grinding demonstrations, readings from A Christmas Carol and holiday crafts. Guests under 18 must come with an adult. The mill is owned by the Forest Preserve District of DuPage County and sits on Salt Creek, where it first opened in 1852.
Can we take a train for Christmas near Oak Brook?

Yes. Metra stops in neighboring Hinsdale on the BNSF line and in Elmhurst on the Union Pacific West line, both with trains to downtown Chicago. For a Santa train, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express. Both sell tickets ahead of time.
